evidence.title: Node.js End-of-Life: Dates, Risks & What to Do Next
evidence.content:
Node.js 20 reaches end of life on April 30, 2026. For a version that entered Active LTS in October 2023, it has seen broad adoption in production environments. However, from May 1, 2026, any vulnerability discovered in Node.js 20 won’t receive an official patch. Given how widely it’s deployed, it is likely to remain an active target for researchers and threat actors when new CVEs surface affecting this version. [...] For teams that need more time to execute their upgrade strategy to a supported LTS release, TuxCare’s Endless Lifecycle Support (ELS) provides continued security patches for version numbers beyond their official end-of-life date. TuxCare currently supports Node.js versions 12, 14, 16, 18, and 20, delivering security patches for as long as your team needs them. This keeps your systems and applications protected and compliant while you execute a migration on a timeline that makes sense for your [...] This is already the reality for teams running Node.js versions 12, 14, 16, or 18, all of which have passed their EOL dates. The Node.js 20 end-of-life date follows on April 30, 2026. If you haven’t planned for this yet, the time is running out.

This article covers what Node EOL means, the exact dates you need to know, the risks of running an unsupported version, and the options available to your team – including how to stay secure if an upgrade is not on the table right now.

evidence.title: Node.js Version Support: EOL Dates and Latest Releases (July 2026)
evidence.content:
The only fully supported lines today are Node.js 26 (Current), 24 (Active LTS), and 22 (Maintenance LTS). Everything else is end-of-life.

‍

## Versions Reaching EOL Next: What to Watch

### Node.js 20 End of Life

Node.js 20 reached end-of-life on April 30, 2026. It was one of the most widely deployed LTS lines in Node's history, which means a large installed base is now running an unsupported runtime. [...] | Version | Release Date | Entered LTS | End of Life | Status |
 ---  --- 
| Node.js 26 | May 5, 2026 | Oct 28, 2026(planned) | Apr 30, 2029 | Current |
| Node.js 25 | Oct 15, 2025 | N/A (odd) | Jun 1, 2026 | EOL |
| Node.js 24 | May 6, 2025 | Oct 28, 2025 | Apr 30, 2028 | Active LTS |
| Node.js 23 | Oct 16, 2024 | N/A (odd) | Jun 1, 2025 | EOL |
| Node.js 22 | Apr 24, 2024 | Oct 29, 2024 | Apr 30, 2027 | Maintenance LTS |
| Node.js 21 | Oct 17, 2023 | N/A (odd) | Jun 1, 2024 | EOL | [...] Node.js 24 is the Active LTS line (EOL April 30, 2028) and Node.js 22 is in Maintenance LTS (EOL April 30, 2027). Node.js 26, released in May 2026, is the Current line and is scheduled to enter LTS in October 2026.

#### Why should I avoid odd-numbered Node.js versions in production?

Odd-numbered releases (19, 21, 23, 25) never enter LTS. They stay Current for six months and then go straight to EOL, so they receive no long-term security support. Use even-numbered LTS lines for production.
